title: A control request spelled as the reserved messagetype is answered in both spellings

provenance.quote: If a NLIP end-point receives a message which has the control field set to true, it must respond with a NLIP Message with control field set to true.

notes: Two fields come back where the peer sent one, and that asymmetry is the reading. §6.3 names the boolean and only the boolean — "must respond with a NLIP Message with control field set to true" — so the boolean is set whichever spelling arrived; setting it is obeying the clause literally, not inventing a field. `messagetype` is then copied from the request rather than composed, so a peer that wrote `CONTROL` would be answered `CONTROL`: §5 makes the value case-insensitive, and rewriting it would be a change the peer can see and the standard did not ask for. The message-level pair is `ecma-430/24` and `/25`, and `readings/22` is where the two spellings disagree inside one message.
